faqLeft.q: What engine does the Jaguar XJ6 use?
faqLeft.a: The XJ6 uses the AJ16 — a 3.2‑ to 4.0‑litre inline‑6 petrol engine. It was fitted from 1994 to 2003 across the X300 and X308 generations.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Jaguar XJ6 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £3,200 for the AJ16. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed‑price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my XJ6?
faqLeft.a: All XJ6 models use the AJ16. We’ll confirm your exact spec by registration to ensure we quote the right parts.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild AJ16 XJ6 engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We rebuild the AJ16 to a near‑new standard, replacing worn components with updated OEM parts, and back it with a 12‑month unlimited‑mileage warranty.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used XJ6 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low‑mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we’ve matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my XJ6 if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an XJ6 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3‑5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most XJ6 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit’s history, and comes with a 12‑month unlimited‑mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.

form.guarantee: Most quotes returned within 30 minutes during working hours.
